title: Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage: Amount of a Bank Draft toward the Resident's Coinsurance Charge
content:
**Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage — applied charge.** A bank-draft payment the resident or representative makes during the call is applied to the resident's original coinsurance charge for the coverage's latest booked coinsurance block, that is, among the coverage's booked-days entries in the band of benefit days 21 through 100 the one whose last service date is the latest, and it settles the resident's share of the settled block's covered days less the payments already applied to that charge.

**Record test.** The bank draft is worked out only for a settled block that passes this record test: its service month carries one booked-days entry in the band of benefit days 21 through 100; at most one such entry of the coverage has the last benefit day just before the settled block's first benefit day; the bed-hold records book at most one leave for its service month and take back none of that leave's held days; its booked-days entry carries at most one day reversal for each reason and none for a booking error; no hospital-day or leave-of-absence reversal on it covers a held night of that leave, and each such reversal counts every day of its span; an uncertified-day reversal on it counts every day of its span except the held nights and the hospital-day and leave-of-absence days inside the span; and, when the supplemental effective date falls after the settled block's first service date, the block before it either has a resident charge billing exactly 100, 50 or 25 percent of that charge's own days times its own daily rate, to within half a percentage point, or carries a secondary charge and no resident charge; and, when the resident's charge for the settled block stands, its day count equals the settled block's booked days less the days of every day reversal posted against its booked-days entry on or before the date that charge was posted; and no hospital-day or leave-of-absence reversal on that entry was posted after the date that charge was posted; and the settled block's last service date falls in 2024 or later, and the charge's open balance is above nothing. The block before the settled block is the coverage's booked-days entry in the band of benefit days 21 through 100 whose last benefit day is the day before the settled block's first benefit day; its resident charge is the resident coinsurance charge posted for it that is not a rebill of a denied secondary share.

For a block that passes its record test, the resident coinsurance charge, the card payment, the rate-year correction, the reduction for reversed covered days and the bank draft each count the days before the supplemental effective date as their own policies state, and only for such a block; for every other block, the tier that sets the split is the one in effect on the days of service: a Medigap policy changes the split from the carrier's policy effective date and QMB protection from the first day of the month after the state's QMB determination, so days before the supplemental effective date keep the earlier split, and none of these five figures is priced for it.

### Terms of the bank draft

- **Rate and earlier share.** The bank draft prices each day it counts at the daily coinsurance rate of 217.00, and days before the supplemental effective date take the earlier share of 100 percent.
- **Supplemental effective date.** The supplemental effective date the bank draft reads is the one recorded on the coverage; a coverage that records none has the tier on file in effect on every day of the settled block.
- **Days counted and payments netted.** The bank draft counts the settled block's covered days, which are its booked days less every day reversed against its booked-days entry; the rounded figure less the payments already applied to the resident's charge, net of any returned payments, is the bank draft, never less than nothing.
- **Days before the date.** The days the bank draft counts before the supplemental effective date are first its calendar days of the settled block before that date: when the date falls after the settled block's first service date and on or before its last, the days from the first service date up to the day before the date; when it falls after the last service date, every calendar day of the settled block; otherwise none. The days the bank draft counts before the supplemental effective date never number fewer than none nor more than the days the bank draft counts.
- **Shares.** Days the bank draft counts before the supplemental effective date take the earlier share; every other day it counts takes the resident share of the tier on file. The resident share of the tier on file is that tier's resident share percent in the cost-sharing split schedule. When the tier on file prohibits balance billing, as the QMB Medicaid Crossover tier does, the bank draft bills the resident nothing for any day on or after the tier's supplemental effective date, those days taking the tier's resident share of nothing, while days before that date keep the earlier split, QMB protection not reaching back before it.
- **Rounding.** The bank draft adds, over the days it counts, the daily rate times the share each day takes, divides the sum by 100 and rounds it half up to the cent once.
- **Open balance.** A bank draft worked out above the resident's charge's open balance, which is its amount less the payments and adjustments posted against it plus any returned payments, shows that the charge was billed below what its days call for; the bank draft is then not taken under this policy, and any payment the payer sends is applied only up to that open balance, the remainder being returned.

### Hypothetical worked example

A coverage moved from the Medigap Plan A or B tier to the QMB Medicaid Crossover tier (resident share 0 percent) after a QMB determination in June 2026, so 1 July 2026 is its supplemental effective date. The settled block runs from 1 June to 24 June 2026: 24 booked days, none reversed; the May block before carries a resident charge billing 100 percent of its own days times its own daily rate, and the settled block passes its record test. 1208.00 has been applied to the resident's charge, nothing returned, and the charge's open balance is 4000.00.

| Step of the definition | Value |
|---|---|
| Days before the date (every calendar day of the block, the date falling after its last service date), earlier share 100 percent | 24 |
| Days on or after the date, share 0 percent | 0 |
| 217.00 times 24 times 100 | 520800 |
| Divided by 100, rounded half up once | 5208.00 |
| Less net payments of 1208.00 | 4000.00 |
| Not above the open balance of 4000.00 | Bank draft **4000.00** |
